sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》（The Psychology of Your 20s），在这里我们探讨二十岁时面临的一些重大生活变化和转变，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目。

sentences.en: Today, I think I am possibly the most excited for this guest of all of our guests this season, because as you know, we love an evidence-based background.
sentences.zh: 今天，对于本季的所有嘉宾，我可能对这位嘉宾感到最兴奋，因为如你所知，我们喜欢基于证据的背景。

sentences.en: We love an informed gueSt.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢有见解的嘉宾。

sentences.en: We love an actual scientific opinion in this space.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢这个领域真正具有科学性的观点。

sentences.en: And I think this person does all of those things.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这个人完全具备这些。

sentences.en: So we have Dr. David Rosmarin, who is an associate professor at Harvard Medical School
sentences.zh: 所以我们请到了大卫·罗斯马林（David Rosmarin）博士，他是哈佛医学院的副教授，

sentences.en: and the founder of the Center for Anxiety, which provides services to over 1,000 patients a year, I think.
sentences.zh: 也是焦虑症中心（Center for Anxiety）的创始人，我想该中心每年为一千多名患者提供服务。

sentences.en: So he is incredible.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常了不起。

sentences.en: He works a lot in, obviously, mental health and a lot around anxiety.
sentences.zh: 他显然在心理健康领域做了大量工作，尤其聚焦于焦虑症。

sentences.en: And he's also been featured in a number of amazing journals that we use on this podcast all the time.
sentences.zh: 他还登上过许多我们在本播客中经常引用的精彩学术期刊。

sentences.en: He's here today to talk about people's anxiety, their experience of anxiety, particularly in their 20s.
sentences.zh: 他今天来到这里，是来谈谈人们的焦虑，他们对焦虑的体验，特别是在二十岁时期的体验。

sentences.en: So welcome.
sentences.zh: 欢迎。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me on your show.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我上你的节目。

sentences.en: It's a great honor and pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 来到这里我感到非常荣幸和高兴。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm really, really excited, actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，其实我真的、真的很兴奋。

sentences.en: I'm super pumped because I feel like maybe we should start firstly with letting you introduce yourself before I jump straight into my line of questioning.
sentences.zh: 我超级激动，因为我觉得也许我们应该首先让你做个自我介绍，然后我再直接抛出一系列问题。

sentences.en: Maybe talk about your journey to where you are now, why you took an interest in this particular area of research, this particular field as well.
sentences.zh: 也许可以谈谈你是如何走到今天的，为什么会对这个特定的研究领域和专业方向产生兴趣。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Well, I myself have definitely struggled with a good deal of anxiety over the years
sentences.zh: 嗯，多年来我自己确实也经历过相当程度的焦虑，

sentences.en: and learning to deal with that, especially somebody who helps others and who does research in this topic
sentences.zh: 学会如何应对这些焦虑，特别是作为一个经常帮助别人、研究这个课题的人，

sentences.en: and who now, you know, my clinics, like you mentioned, we're servicing over a thousand people every year, has been so positive.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所提到的，现在我的诊所每年服务超过一千人，这段经历真的是太棒了。

sentences.en: It's been such a blessing for me to be able to have these challenging experiences.
sentences.zh: 能够拥有这些充满挑战的经历，对我来说真是一种福气。

sentences.en: I'm not going to say that anxiety is fun.
sentences.zh: 我不会说焦虑是件有趣的事。

sentences.en: It is not.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: Nobody likes it.
sentences.zh: 没有人喜欢它。

sentences.en: It's so uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 它是如此令人不适。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing that we want to get rid of.
sentences.zh: 这是那种我们想要摆脱的东西。

sentences.en: But the times in my life when I've had that have made me so able to connect with my patients and in some ways more resilient.
sentences.zh: 但生命中经历这些的时刻，让我能够如此感同身受地走近我的患者，并在某种程度上变得更有韧性。

sentences.en: And I actually think today that anxiety can be a great catalyst for growth and for thriving if we use the right tools and approaches in order to get there.
sentences.zh: 而且我今天甚至认为，如果我们使用正确的工具和方法去面对，焦虑可以成为成长和蓬勃发展的巨大催化剂。

sentences.en: Yeah, I love that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很喜欢这个观点。

sentences.en: I think often people talk about these things without having a personal experience with them, which can be so frustrating.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多人在谈论这些事情时，自己并没有切身体验，这往往会让人感到沮丧。

sentences.en: But I do think that that shared vulnerability, that shared experience is a bit of a unifier, a bit of a superpower.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，这种共同的脆弱感和共同的经历，是一种凝聚力，也是一种超能力。

sentences.en: You know, I appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我很感激这一点。

sentences.en: Now, let me ask you a question.
sentences.zh: 现在，我来问你一个问题。

sentences.en: Have you ever met anybody who didn't have anxiety before?
sentences.zh: 你有没有见过从来没有焦虑过的人？

sentences.en: It's so funny that you asked me this because I think I've met a couple and one of them is actually my partner and he I'm going to I'm going to share all here.
sentences.zh: 你问我这个真的很有趣，因为我想我确实见过几个，其中一个其实是我的伴侣，而我——我要在这里全盘托出了。

sentences.en: He's got a pretty stressful job.
sentences.zh: 他的工作压力挺大的。

sentences.en: He's a solicitor.
sentences.zh: 他是一名诉讼律师。

sentences.en: He's a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他是个律师。

sentences.en: And I've never seen that man anxious.
sentences.zh: 但我从来没见那个男人焦虑过。

sentences.en: He'll be up till 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 他可以一直忙到凌晨两点。

sentences.en: Never.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: And I think it's the yin and yang, right?
sentences.zh: 我想这就是阴阳互补吧？

sentences.en: But in general, I know you are you're expecting a different answer.
sentences.zh: 不过总的来说，我知道你期待的是另一个答案。

sentences.en: It's very few if and far between the individuals who have never had anxiety before.
sentences.zh: 从来没有过焦虑的人是非常少之又少的。

sentences.en: And I think one of the biggest issues and one of the reasons anxiety gets out of control is that often we judge ourselves and we get very upset when we start to feel anxious,
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的问题之一，也是焦虑失控的原因之一，往往是我们开始感到焦虑时，会去自我评判并感到非常沮丧，

sentences.en: as opposed to realizing that this is a very human emotion.
sentences.zh: 而不是意识到这其实是一种非常人类的情感。

sentences.en: This is the kind of thing that's going to happen to the vast majority of people, except for your
sentences.zh: 这是绝大多数人都会经历的事情，除了你的

sentences.en: partner and everyone, almost everyone at some point is going to butt up against these feelings, these sensations, and they're uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 伴侣之外，几乎每个人在某个时刻都会不可避免地触碰到这些感受和体验，它们确实令人不适。

sentences.en: We want to get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 我们想要摆脱它。

sentences.en: But, you know, learning to grapple with it and to parlay that into positive ways in our life is really the name of the game, as opposed to trying to squelch it and combat it.
sentences.zh: 但是，学会与它搏斗并将之转化为生活中积极的动力，才是解决问题的关键，而不是试图去压制和对抗它。

sentences.en: I think that really personally relates to me as well.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这跟我个人的经历也很有共鸣。

sentences.en: The times I've been most anxious is when I've been asking myself to be least anxious, when I've really been suppressing that feeling because it, you know, wasn't comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我最焦虑的时候，反而是我要求自己不要焦虑的时候，当我真的在压抑那种感觉的时候，因为你知道，那很不舒服。

sentences.en: It wasn't it wasn't necessary at the time.
sentences.zh: 那时候它很不合时宜、没有必要。

sentences.en: I felt like it was interrupting other things in my life, but I do kind of want to just quickly start at the basics because I feel like when it comes to anxiety, there is somewhat
sentences.zh: 我觉得它打乱了我生活中的其他事情，但我确实想先从基础知识快速切入，因为我觉得当谈到焦虑时，多多少少

sentences.en: a bit of misinformation around there.
sentences.zh: 存在一些错误的信息。

sentences.en: Sometimes people, you know, I think people love to self-diagnose.
sentences.zh: 有时人们，我觉得人们很喜欢自我诊断。

sentences.en: People love to throw terms around like I'm just so, you know, I've just got such bad anxiety.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢抛出一些词汇，比如“我只是太……你知道的，我焦虑得太严重了”。

sentences.en: I've got such bad OCD.
sentences.zh: “我有很严重的强迫症。”

sentences.en: I've got such bad social anxiety, social phobia, whatever it may be.
sentences.zh: “我有很严重的社交焦虑、社交恐惧症，诸如此类。”

sentences.en: So can we just quickly strip back to the basics?
sentences.zh: 所以我们能快速回归基础吗？

sentences.en: What exactly is not just anxiety, but some of the distinctions within the broader anxiety
sentences.zh: 究竟什么是焦虑？不仅仅是泛指焦虑，还包括更广泛的焦虑领域中

sentences.en: space, you know, perhaps between a panic disorder, social anxiety, generalized anxiety, not everyone obviously experiences it the same way.
sentences.zh: 的一些区别，比如恐慌症、社交焦虑、广泛性焦虑之间有什么不同？显然并不是每个人都有相同的体验。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you strip it down when you want to define anxiety, you really have to start with fear.
sentences.zh: 如果你剥茧抽丝来定义焦虑，你真的必须从恐惧开始谈起。

sentences.en: Now, fear is a healthy emotion that everybody, almost everyone, is programmed with, which involves adrenaline.
sentences.zh: 现在，恐惧是一种健康的本能，几乎每个人生来就带有这种设定，它涉及肾上腺素。

sentences.en: Adrenaline gets pumped into your bloodstream the minute you perceive a threat.
sentences.zh: 当你感知到威胁的那一刻，肾上腺素就会被泵入你的血液中。

sentences.en: And the fear response, otherwise known as the fight or flight response, is a healthy adaptation which helps you to survive.
sentences.zh: 恐惧反应，也就是人们常知的“战斗或逃跑反应”（fight or flight response），是一种有助于你生存的健康适应机制。

sentences.en: So you'll either flee or fight or freeze if you're in a certain situation and you're more likely to survive those situations.
sentences.zh: 所以身处某种特定情境时，你要么逃跑，要么战斗，要么呆立不动，这样你在那些情境下存活下来的几率会更高。

sentences.en: Babies, neonates, who do not have a fight or flight response, they usually don't survive.
sentences.zh: 婴儿，也就是新生儿，如果不具备战斗或逃跑反应，他们通常无法存活。

sentences.en: They usually will not survive beyond 30 days.
sentences.zh: 他们通常无法活过30天。

sentences.en: It's a neurological problem, in fact, if people don't have that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果人们没有这种反应，那其实是一个神经系统的问题。

sentences.en: Now, what's anxiety?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是焦虑呢？

sentences.en: Anxiety is the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 焦虑完全是一回事。

sentences.en: It shares the same brain circuitry.
sentences.zh: 它共享相同的脑回路。

sentences.en: It shares the same neurobiology as fear.
sentences.zh: 它与恐惧拥有相同的神经生物学基础。

sentences.en: However, there's one key difference.
sentences.zh: 然而，有一个关键的区别。

sentences.en: It's a false alarm.
sentences.zh: 它是一个误报（false alarm）。

sentences.en: So fear would be a real alarm, like, oh, no, I really have to get out of the way of this bus, which is careening towards me down to City Street.
sentences.zh: 所以恐惧是真实的警报，比如：天哪，我必须赶快躲开这辆正朝我疾驰而来的城市公交车。

sentences.en: And anxiety would be, I'm in this social situation and I feel afraid.
sentences.zh: 而焦虑则是：我身处这个社交场合，我感到害怕。

sentences.en: My fear response is going off, but it's unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 我的恐惧反应被触发了，但这是不必要的。

sentences.en: Now, I want to clarify.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想澄清一下。

sentences.en: In other words, like I said, it's a false alarm.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就像我说的，这是一次误报。

sentences.en: So I want to clarify, you are going to have false alarMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我想澄清，你确实会经历误报。

sentences.en: You're going to have them sometimes.
sentences.zh: 你有时会经历这些。

sentences.en: If, you know, sometimes in your kitchen or wherever it is, you're going to have, you know, your smoke alarm is going to go off.
sentences.zh: 如果，你知道的，有时在你的厨房或其他地方，你会遇到烟雾报警器突然响起来的情况。

sentences.en: And that's good.
sentences.zh: 这其实是好事。

sentences.en: That actually indicates that the batteries are working, the circuitry is working, and you have the protective factor in there, in place, the protective mechanism in place
sentences.zh: 这实际上表明电池还在工作，电路在运转，并且你体内已经具备了一种保护机制

sentences.en: that if there were a fire, it would wake you up and it would save your life.
sentences.zh: ——即如果真的发生火灾，它能把你唤醒并救你一命。

sentences.en: That's much better than what's deadly with the smoke alarm is batteries when the batteries die or when you don't have it.
sentences.zh: 这远比烟雾报警器电池耗尽或形同虚设那种致命情况要好得多。

sentences.en: So anxiety just shows you that it's actually working, but it's a, it's a misfire of the fear system.
sentences.zh: 所以焦虑只是向你展示它确实在工作，只不过是恐惧系统的一次误触发。

sentences.en: Can I ask you a question?
sentences.zh: 我能问你一个问题吗？

sentences.en: Because there's, which is kind of going back a little bit, but it's something that people ask me about all the time.

sentences.zh: 我认为这也是一种逃避冲突的趋势，就像想要避开各种各样的冲突一样。

sentences.en: It's not easy, but it's an important skill that I don't think we practice enough.
sentences.zh: 我在自己的生活中也看到过这一点，也许还有那种讨好型人格的倾向，我认为我们这一代人这种倾向要多得多，为了不冒犯别人。

sentences.en: I think it's also this trend of conflict aversion as well, like wanting to avoid all kinds of conflict.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对于20多岁的年轻人来说，讨好型行为要比我20岁时多得多。

sentences.en: I've seen that in my own life, perhaps that people pleasing tendency as well, which I think our generation has a lot more of, not to offend.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I think there is a lot more people pleasing in for people, for folks in their 20s than there was when I was, when I was 20.
sentences.zh: 但我想问你这个问题，因为这是我超级着迷的、夹在中间的核心部分，那就是：你认为我们治疗焦虑的方法发生了怎样的变化？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 而且我要说的是，我对你这种哲学，对你对此可能持有的观点的着迷，其实显得我有点自私。

sentences.en: But I want to ask you this question because this is the thing I think kind of the main part
sentences.zh: 它源于我个人的经历。

sentences.en: of the sandwich here that I'm super fascinated by, which is how do you think that our approach to treating anxiety has changed?
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道的，焦虑的过度医疗化。

sentences.en: And I'm going to say my fascination with this, you know, with this philosophy that you have with perhaps your opinion on this is quite selfish of me.
sentences.zh: 我很小的时候就被诊断出患有焦虑症。

sentences.en: It comes from a personal place.
sentences.zh: 它一直是我生活中的常态，听起来在你的生活中也是如此。

sentences.en: It's, you know, the over-medicalization of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 在我19岁的时候，我开始服用来士普（Lexapro），这是一种兼具抗焦虑和抗抑郁作用的药物，而且我还很快被开了安定（Valium），不过我现在已经不用了。

sentences.en: I was diagnosed with anxiety when I was quite young.
sentences.zh: 所以我想通过我的这些行为，我某种程度上从这种更加偏向医疗、生物医学的方法中受益了。

sentences.en: It's been a constant in my life as it sounds like it has been in yours.
sentences.zh: 但你说我们可以用不同的方式来做事。

sentences.en: And when I was 19, I went on Lexapro, which is kind of a dual anxiety, depression medication was also like very quickly prescribed Valium, which I no longer use.
sentences.zh: 显然，我这不是在向你征求个人的医疗建议。

sentences.en: And so I guess by way of my actions, I've kind of benefited from this more medical, biomedical approach.
sentences.zh: 那将是非常不合适的，但更多的是说：这意味着什么？

sentences.en: But you say that we can do things differently.
sentences.zh: 这种不同的方法是什么？

sentences.en: And obviously, this is not me asking you for personal medical advice.
sentences.zh: 我们怎么能用不同的方式来做到这一点，而不是去吃一把有时人们以为会是奇迹、能改变他们一生的药丸呢？

sentences.en: That would be entirely inappropriate, but more in the sense of like, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: What is this different approach?
sentences.zh: 首先也是最重要的一点，我绝不反对药物治疗。

sentences.en: How could we do this differently without perhaps taking a pill that sometimes people think is going to be this miracle, this one thing that is going to change their life?
sentences.zh: 而且我确实看到，可以说超过50%的患者都在使用药物治疗、使用精神科药物。

sentences.en: Great questions.
sentences.zh: 只要是带着某种意图服用的，我是支持这一点的。

sentences.en: First and foremost, I'm not against pharmacology in any way.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不知道你19岁开始吃来士普时别人对你说了什么，但你先是吃了来士普，接着又吃了安定，这个事实表明，情况可能

sentences.en: And I do see, I would say more than 50% of my patients use pharmacology, use medicine, psychiatric medications.
sentences.zh: 大致是这样的：“我要吃这个来减轻我的焦虑，这样我才能应付日常生活并能够克服它。”

sentences.en: And I'm a supporter of that as long as it's taken with certain intent.
sentences.zh: 如果服用来士普时，你的意图是“我需要摆脱这些感觉，我再也不想有这种感觉了”，首先，这是行不通的。

sentences.en: Now, I don't know what you were told when you were 19 and put on Lexapro, but the fact that you were put on Lexapro first and Valium second indicates that probably it was something
sentences.zh: 没有任何药物能消除你的焦虑，因为如果它能的话，它就会消除你的恐惧反应，那其实是不适应环境的。

sentences.en: along the lines of, I'm going to take this in order to reduce my anxiety so I can manage day to day and be able to overcome it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: If the Lexapro, if your intent was I would need to get rid of these feelings and I cannot have them ever again, firstly, that doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 首先，我并不反对药物治疗。

sentences.en: There's no medication that will take away your anxiety because if it could, it would take away your fear response, which would actually be maladaptive.
sentences.zh: 而且据我估计，超过50%的患者都在使用药物治疗。

sentences.en: That would not be healthy for you at a neural level, at an emotional level, behaviorally or in any other way.
sentences.zh: 无论是神经层面、情感层面、行为层面，还是在其他任何层面上，这对你都是不健康的。

sentences.en: We need people's fear systems to be in place so that you can be protected if you need it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要人们的恐惧系统发挥作用，这样在必要时你才能得到保护。

sentences.en: So we're not going to strip that down.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会把它剥离掉。

sentences.en: There would be catastrophic consequences if that were the case.
sentences.zh: 如果真是那样，会产生灾难性的后果。

sentences.en: But what can be done is to tamp it down a little bit so that a person has enough anxiety that they can tolerate.
sentences.zh: 但可以做的是把它稍微压制一下，好让一个人承受适度的焦虑。

sentences.en: Sometimes people's anxiety gets so high that they just cannot tolerate it.
sentences.zh: 有时人们的焦虑会变得如此之高，以至于他们根本无法承受。

sentences.en: They can't use it to thrive in a positive way in their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们无法利用它在生活中积极地蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: So we need to pharmacologically reduce it to a regular level.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要通过药物将它降到一个正常的水平。

sentences.en: Now, benzodiazepines, Valium, Ativan, Valium, Klonopin, and the like are completely different.
sentences.zh: 苯二氮䓬类药物，比如安定、阿提凡、氯硝西泮之类，则完全不同。

sentences.en: They work on a different brain system called GABA.
sentences.zh: 它们作用于一个叫做GABA的不同大脑系统。

sentences.en: And what those do is they sort of immediately reduce your anxiety.
sentences.zh: 它们的作用基本上是立即减轻你的焦虑。

sentences.en: Xanax is your classic one, right?
sentences.zh: 阿普唑仑就是最典型的代表，对吧？

sentences.en: They immediately reduce your anxiety.
sentences.zh: 它们能立即减轻你的焦虑。

sentences.en: Now, often people are given those as a first-line treatment, and I do not think that's, in general, in general, I don't think that's a wise practice.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们通常会被作为一线治疗方案给予这类药物，而我认为总体而言，这并不是一种明智的做法。

sentences.en: I don't think that's a wise medical practice.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不是一种明智的医疗做法。

sentences.en: Because what ends up happening is people assume, the minute I feel anxious, they're taking this
sentences.zh: 因为最后发生的情况是，人们一感到焦虑，就会认为

sentences.en: fast-acting medication.
sentences.zh: 这是一种见效快的药物。

sentences.en: Lexapro is slower-acting over time.
sentences.zh: 来士普则是随着时间慢慢起效的。

sentences.en: So it'll reduce your anxiety over a period of four to six weeks to a reasonable level, and then you can reduce it over time if you want.
sentences.zh: 所以它会在四周到六周的时间内将你的焦虑降到一个合理的水平，然后如果你愿意，随着时间推移你可以减少药量。

sentences.en: You can reduce your dose and then tolerate higher levels.
sentences.zh: 你可以减少剂量，然后去承受更高程度的焦虑。

sentences.en: With benzos, it's a different game.
sentences.zh: 对于苯二氮䓬类药物，情况就完全不同了。

sentences.en: And that approach is really, in some ways, reinforcing the idea, I shouldn't feel anxious.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这种方法实际上在强化这样一种观念：我不应该感到焦虑。

sentences.en: I don't want to ever feel anxious.
sentences.zh: 我永远不想感到焦虑。

sentences.en: I have to get rid of this anxiety or something catastrophic will happen.
sentences.zh: 我必须摆脱这种焦虑，否则就会发生灾难性的事情。

sentences.en: And all of those messages just sensitize us further.
sentences.zh: 所有这些信息只会让我们变得更加敏感。

sentences.en: Often, and I've seen this in hundreds of cases, where people were told by a pharmacologist, you need to take this Xanax or whatever it is, in order to cope with their anxiety, it
sentences.zh: 通常情况下——我在数百个案例中都见过这种情况——当人们被药物学家告知，为了应对焦虑，你需要服用阿普唑仑或诸如此类的药物，它

sentences.en: will take it away.
sentences.zh: 会消除这种焦虑。

sentences.en: And it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And then they feel even worse about themselves the next time their anxiety goes higher.
sentences.zh: 结果，当下一次焦虑加剧时，他们对自己的感觉会变得更加糟糕。

sentences.en: And they end up on three, four, or five medications.
sentences.zh: 他们最终得服用三种、四种甚至五种药物。

sentences.en: Then, you know, it can get very complicated very quickly.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，情况很快就会变得非常复杂。

sentences.en: I find that very personally relevant.
sentences.zh: 我发现这对我个人很有切身体会。

sentences.en: That made a lot of sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说非常有道理。

sentences.en: I think it's also something I realized.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是我意识到的事情。

sentences.en: I used to have a really terrible fear of flying, terrible claustrophobia, and that's why I used Valium.
sentences.zh: 我过去对坐飞机有非常严重的恐惧，有严重的幽闭恐惧症，这就是我以前使用安定（Valium）的原因。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: The fear response was not there, but the level of avoidance that I had towards the activity increased like crazy because I became more fearful of that fear response, right?
sentences.zh: 恐惧反应虽然没有出现，但我对这种活动的逃避程度却呈指数级增长，因为我变得更加害怕那种恐惧反应了，对吧？

sentences.en: Because I was teaching myself that it was so dangerous, that it was so scary, that I was so unable to cope, that I needed to be taking this medication at higher doses.
sentences.zh: 因为我在教导自己：它是如此危险，如此可怕，我是如此无力应对，以至于我需要服用更高剂量的这种药物。

sentences.en: What did you think would happen?
sentences.zh: 你觉得会发生什么？

sentences.en: What did you think would happen if you just let your anxiety go?
sentences.zh: 如果你任由焦虑顺其自然，你觉得会发生什么？

sentences.en: Oh, I had some crazy irrational fears.
sentences.zh: 哦，我当时有一些疯狂的非理性恐惧。

sentences.en: That's the other part about, you know, I think anxiety is quite irrational, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是另一方面，你知道的，我认为焦虑是非常不理智的，对吧？

sentences.en: And it was, you know, if I was on this plane and I wasn't taking Valium, I was going to have a panic attack and I was going to try and rip open the doors of the plane because I was
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，如果我在飞机上没有服用安定，我会惊恐发作，我会试图去疯狂地推开飞机的舱门，因为我

sentences.en: so scared.
sentences.zh: 太害怕了。

sentences.en: I was like, is this a possibility?
sentences.zh: 当时我在想，这有可能吗？

sentences.en: Could I completely, could I seriously hurt other passengers on board?
sentences.zh: 我真的会完全失控、严重伤害机上的其他乘客吗？

sentences.en: Or I think worrying about embarrassing myself and, and then I think I examined the fear further and I was like,
sentences.zh: 或者我在担心让自己出丑，然后我觉得自己进一步审视了这种恐惧，我想的是……

sentences.en: and the thing I always say for people to do is, is this so what?
sentences.zh: 我总是对人们说的一句话是，那又怎样？

sentences.en: So you have a panic attack on the plane, so what?
sentences.zh: 所以你在飞机上惊恐发作了，那又怎样？

sentences.en: So I'm going to embarrass myself, so what?
sentences.zh: 所以我出丑了，那又怎样？

sentences.en: I think the thing that I realized in that, and you say this and you said it before and I love, love this phrase.
sentences.zh: 我想我在其中意识到的一点是——你经常说，而且你以前也说过，我太喜欢、太喜欢这个短语了。

sentences.en: You have to get comfortable with being uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 你必须学会习惯不适感。

sentences.en: How do you think we get there?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们该如何做到这一点？

sentences.en: Because being uncomfortable is not something that we particularly enjoy doing.
sentences.zh: 因为感到不舒服并不是我们特别喜欢做的事。

sentences.en: Nobody likes it, but it's going to happen sometimes and we do have to get used to it.
sentences.zh: 没人喜欢这样，但这种情况有时确实会发生，我们必须习惯它。

sentences.en: Now, the question is how much discomfort can we, when we, listen, I feel anxious throughout, I wouldn't say on a weekly basis, certainly a couple of times a month, something comes
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，当我们承受多少不适时……听着，我一直都会感到焦虑，我不会说每周都这样，但肯定一个月有好几次，总会有事情

sentences.en: up that makes me feel viscerally uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 发生，让我感到由衷的不适。

sentences.en: And when my stress level is high, I'm more likely to have that.
sentences.zh: 当我的压力水平很高时，这种情况就更有可能发生。

sentences.en: I'll tell you what I do.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你我是怎么做的。

sentences.en: I'll be very autobiographical here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里说点非常私人的经历。

sentences.en: I lean right into it.
sentences.zh: 我直接迎上去。

sentences.en: I'm feeling terrible right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在感觉糟糕透了。

sentences.en: What am I upset about?
sentences.zh: 我在为什麽心烦？

sentences.en: And I bring it on.
sentences.zh: 我把它招惹出来。

sentences.en: I think right towards it.
sentences.zh: 我径直面对它。

sentences.en: And if I'm feeling, if something makes me feel more uncomfortable, I will gravitate even more towards it.
sentences.zh: 如果我感觉……如果有什么事让我感到更加不适，我会更倾向于迎向它。

sentences.en: I'll talk about it in great detail with people, get it off my chest, embrace it, let the fear wash over me.
sentences.zh: 我会和别人极其详细地谈论它，一吐为快，拥抱它，让恐惧感将我淹没。

sentences.en: It is, it's sort of like ripping off a band-aid.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是揭掉创可贴。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Just like, we're going to do this.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我们要这么做。

sentences.en: It's really freaking hard.
sentences.zh: 这真的难得要命。

sentences.en: Do it.
sentences.zh: 去做吧。

sentences.en: And it hurts.
sentences.zh: 这很痛苦。

sentences.en: It really hurts.
sentences.zh: 真的很痛。

sentences.en: It's bad.
sentences.zh: 感觉很糟。

sentences.en: But it, I'll tell you what ends up happening when you lean into it is this, what we talked about before, the parasympathetic nervous system.
sentences.zh: 但是，我告诉你当你迎难而上时最终会发生什么：这就是我们之前谈到的副交感神经系统。

sentences.en: You have wiring and you have chemicals inside of you, which will calm you down.
sentences.zh: 你的体内有神经回路和化学物质，它们能让你平静下来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We see over a thousand patients a year in my practice.
sentences.zh: 我的诊所每年接待一千多名患者。

sentences.en: How many of them have had a panic attack that lasted more than 90 minutes ever?
sentences.zh: 他们当中有多少人曾经历过持续超过90分钟的惊恐发作？

sentences.en: I'm sure it's zero.
sentences.zh: 我敢说肯定是零。

sentences.en: Zero.
sentences.zh: 零。

sentences.en: The number is zero.
sentences.zh: 数字就是零。

sentences.en: And my colleagues who have similarly sized clinics treating tens of thousands of patients on an annual basis for decades, I have spoken with them.
sentences.zh: 我的同行们也有同样规模的诊所，几十年来每年治疗成千上万的患者，我和他们交流过。

sentences.en: And the number of patients who have had a panic attack more than 90 minutes ever.
sentences.zh: 经历过超过90分钟惊恐发作的患者人数是多少？

sentences.en: I'm going to go for the same answer.
sentences.zh: 我的回答还是一样。

sentences.en: It's zero.
sentences.zh: 是零。

sentences.en: How about the number of people who have crashed their car during a panic attack?
sentences.zh: 那么在惊恐发作期间把车开翻的人数呢？

sentences.en: It doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 根本没有发生过这种事。

sentences.en: The number of people who have gotten up in the middle of a plane and started running around and stabbing people with a plastic fork.
sentences.zh: 有人在飞机中间站起来开始四处乱跑，用塑料叉子捅人的情况吗？

sentences.en: Listen, I'm going to say maybe at least one.
sentences.zh: 听着，我可以说至少有一个吧。

sentences.en: I've seen some weird Karen videos, but it probably is zero.
sentences.zh: 我看过一些奇怪的“凯伦”视频，但可能还是零。

sentences.en: Well, there was that one time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，确实有那么一次。

sentences.en: No, I'm kidding.
sentences.zh: 不，我开玩笑的。

sentences.en: The answer is zero.
sentences.zh: 答案是零。

sentences.en: People don't do that.
sentences.zh: 人们不会那样做。

sentences.en: When you're anxious, you're actually more in control of yourself.
sentences.zh: 当你感到焦虑时，你其实对自己的控制力更强。

sentences.en: You're dealing with your own emotions.
sentences.zh: 你在处理自己的情绪。

sentences.en: You're not.
sentences.zh: 你并没有失控。

sentences.en: And often you can't even tell.
sentences.zh: 而且通常你甚至自己都感觉不到。

sentences.en: Like people say, everyone can see I'm anxious.
sentences.zh: 就像人们会说，每个人都能看出我很焦虑。

sentences.en: No, they're looking at themselves.
sentences.zh: 不，他们都在关注他们自己。

sentences.en: They're not looking at you.
sentences.zh: 他们才没看你呢。

sentences.en: What is it called?
sentences.zh: 这叫什么来着？

sentences.en: The spotlight effect?
sentences.zh: 聚光灯效应？

sentences.en: Everything that we do seems to be like super, super obvious to other people, but we're all in our kind of own internal lives and internal minds.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的每一件事在其他人看来似乎都超级、超级明显，但其实我们都活在各自的内心世界和思维中。

sentences.en: That's really interesting because I think that that's a really important reminder to people who experience kind of the shame cycle of like, this is super embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为我认为对于那些经历过“这超级尴尬”这种羞耻循环的人来说，这是一个非常重要的提醒。

sentences.en: The one thing I do and I is really similar to you is like, I tell myself I'm excited by the feeling because I think anxiety and excitement feel very, very similar.
sentences.zh: 我所做的一件事——这真的和你很像——就是我告诉自己，我对这种感觉感到兴奋，因为我认为焦虑和兴奋的感觉非常、非常相似。

sentences.en: So I'm like, this is the most exciting feeling ever.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，这是有史以来最让人兴奋的感觉。

sentences.en: It's actually the same chemical.
sentences.zh: 这其实是同一种化学物质。

sentences.en: It's adrenaline, you know, adrenaline and epinephrine.
sentences.zh: 也就是肾上腺素，你知道的，肾上腺素和去甲肾上腺素。

sentences.en: Those are the chemicals that are secreted when we're excited and when we're anxious.
sentences.zh: 这些就是当我们兴奋和焦虑时分泌的化学物质。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you can just tell yourself that it's something different.
